Consonant clusters are a combination of consonant sounds. These can be difficult to pronounce for some English language learners.
Minimal Pairs are two words that sound similar, except for one sound.
Some examples of consonant clusters are:

sp - special
thr - three
tr - trash
str - straight

To avoid being misunderstood, you should:
  • avoid changing a consonant in a cluster to a different consonant (present/pleasant)
  • avoid leaving out one of the consonant sounds (poblem/problem)
  • avoid adding an extra vowel between consonants (tewin/twin)
  • avoid adding an extra vowel at the beginning of a word (estop/stop)
Practicing minimal pairs is a good way to avoid these problems.

Instructions: Complete the following steps. Fill in the Self-Assessment.

images.text:
Receptionist: Welcome! Are you here to check in?
Adam: Yes. We reserved two rooms. My secretary has also sent a few special requests by e-mail.
Receptionist: Let me see. There's no reservation under either name.
Adam: Impossible. This has been in the works for months. Could you check under BFP, please?
Receptionist: Ahh, there we go. You have one room booked.
Adam: There must have been some mistake. We definitely booked two rooms. I haven't shared a room since I was in college.
Receptionist: It says here that a request was made. It says, “we'd like to share.”
Adam: Chair, not share. It was requested that an office chair be provided, because we are going to be working from the room.

Receptionist: Oh, I see, so you're sure you don't want to share? It might strengthen your working relationship.
Adam: Yes, I'm absolutely sure we don't want to share.
Receptionist: Now, about the clam chowder that was mentioned in your email, we normally don't serve ...
Adam: It says that I wanted a warm shower, not clam chowder! Why in the world would I want clam chowder?
Receptionist: We couldn't figure it out either. And then it was pointed out that you are from Boston. We assumed you must have wanted a little taste of home.
Adam: Well, you assumed wrong, I'm afraid. It must have been an autocorrect mistake. My secretary sent the e-mail from her cellphone.
Receptionist: Right. Now, I notice that a tree tower was mentioned. We have a strict “no tree tower” policy.
Adam: Are you kidding me? I said I want three towels, not a tree tower. What is a tree tower, anyway?

Receptionist: One of our bellhops claimed that it's a sort of tree house, where people from Boston go to eat clam chowder.
Adam: Ummm, no.
Receptionist: Okay, now that we've got that straightened out, here's your key. The thrash band is already in the room, rehearsing.
Adam: A thrash band? Playing thrash metal? In my room! My god, I'm afraid to ask.
Receptionist: It's written here, sir. “One thrash band beside the desk, please.”
Adam: A trash bin, for garbage!
Receptionist: We thought it was a Boston thing.
Adam: Of course you did. Well, thanks anyway.
Receptionist: Did you say tanks? I'm afraid we don't allow those, either.
